newsitem.title: USA: Evita portrait brings world's eye to U.S. museum.
newsitem.headline: Evita portrait brings world's eye to U.S. museum.

text.p: The only portrait Eva Peron was ever known to have sat for has drawn the interest of every auction house and collector in the world, a spokeswoman of a small Florida museum which has the painting on display said on Wednesday.

"Interest has been phenomenal... I'm getting calls every 10 to 15 minutes wanting to know information," said Cathy Lea, communications manager at the Museum of Arts and Sciences in this eastern Florida city.

She said since Tuesday when the museum displayed the oil-on-canvas portrait of Peron by the Brazilian artist Candido Portinari, "There's been an interest by every auction house and collector and everything, it seems like, in the world."
Lea said attendance at the museum has also jumped. About 200 people viewed the portrait on Tuesday and another 100 came on Wednesday, about 30 percent higher than the museum's normal attendance.

Interest in the portrait has been sparked by the film "Evita," based on Andrew Lloyd Webber's musical of the same name, which stars Madonna as Eva Duarte de Peron, the celebrated first lady of Argentina during the populist government of Juan Peron.
Lea said the museum had no plans of selling the painting, done in 1940 when Peron was a 21-year-old radio star.
